children: Better said corporate efficiencies since its Week 6 scorecard are expected to generate $38.97M in annualized savings; it also reported $0.77M in total realized savings toward a $64.2M target. The company is moving toward an agreement to sell Birmingham Bank.
The figure reflects expected annualized savings from corporate efficiencies since Week 6; it is not savings already realized.
Realized savings remain a small portion of the stated target, making execution and timing important to the turnaround.
Moving toward agreement to sell Birmingham Bank
A sale could sharpen the company's focus on its US business, but no signed agreement or sale terms were announced.
Signed mortgage-servicer agreement to offer home equity loans
Adds a channel to reach existing borrowers; the release gives no contract value or quantified revenue impact.
$1.5M in vendor reductions intended by Dec. 1
These reductions are planned, not completed, and would add to cost savings if executed.

This is a weekly update in Better's ongoing turnaround, rather than a completed sale or a report of financial results. Further realized savings, execution of planned cuts, and a signed Birmingham Bank sale agreement would provide the next evidence of progress.
